text: combined_df is one flat table, with CustomerSegment and territory details repeated on every row. That's the wrong shape for a model two different pages need to slice two different ways.
Fact holds the numbers at the original line-level grain. DimCustomer holds one row per customer with its segment label. DimTerritory holds one row per territory with its group.
In Model view, both relationships run one to many, filtering from the dimension side down to Fact: one customer or territory, many fact rows.
Keeping CustomerSegment and TerritoryGroup on their own dimension tables, instead of flattened onto Fact, is what lets an ALL of DimTerritory style measure work cleanly in the next lesson.
With a clean star schema in place, next lesson writes the real DAX measures, including the two benchmark measures both stakeholder pages depend on.
